name: section4b_disk_farkas_thickness_aligned
purpose: Seven extra grid rungs for the disk benchmark, at h = 1.75/n mm. They
were run to test a hypothesis about why marching cubes' patch area moves
backwards under refinement. The hypothesis was falsified by these runs.
The rungs are kept and used, for a different reason than they were run.
status: hypothesis falsified; rungs retained for range and density

observation: On the dyadic ladder marching cubes reads 3.500e-4 m^2 of patch area at
5 mm and 2.940e-4 at 2.5 mm: refinement moving the answer away from the
truth. An analysis gate excluded rungs on that reversal, which left
marching cubes three error points over one factor of four in h.
claim: The isotropic grid spans the disk's 1.75 mm thickness with about 1.75/h
cells, and the rim -- where the area error lives -- is resolved only as
well as that count. The dyadic ladder gives 1, 1, 2, 3, 6, 12 cells: it
repeats one and skips four, five, and seven through eleven. If area is
governed by that count, then h = 1.75/n makes the count strictly
increasing, no reversal is possible, and the gate never fires.
prediction: Two rungs with the same thickness-cell count should read the same area.

the_falsification.test: The denser ladder produces equal-cell-count pairs at different h.
verdict: Equal-cell-count pairs disagree by up to 2.6 percent, and in two of the
three pairs the COARSER rung is closer to exact. Patch area is not a
function of thickness resolution, so the reversals are scatter rather
The gate built on that premise is therefore deleted, not merely unused:
a rule that discards rungs on reversal keeps whichever tail happened to
come out monotone. Do not reinstate it. Marching cubes' rim deficit is
about one cell and resolution-independent, with scatter that remains
unexplained; the phase hypothesis for that scatter is untested and is
deliberately kept out of the paper.
second_failure: Fitting the aligned ladder on its own also fails, for an unrelated
reason: it spans only 6x in h, and per-interval scatter swamps the
slope -- it gave a tetrahedral residual of 0.223 and a marching-cubes
order of -0.485. Range, not sampling density, is what the fit needs.
rounding_caveat_that_materialized: The grid is positioned by the ground box rather than by the disk, so the
thickness spans n or n+1 cells depending on phase. h = 1.75/12 rounded
to 0.145833 gives 13 cells by ceil, not 12. The caveat was recorded
before the run and then happened.

what_the_rungs_are_actually_for: Combined with the dyadic ladder they give 17 tetrahedral rungs over a 250x
span and 13 affine rungs over 32x, which is the range the order fits need.
The analysis now fits all rungs and refuses to name an order unless the
error fell at least tenfold, which is what replaced the gate.

why_not_finer: n = 14 is estimated at 83 GB, past what this machine holds alongside
anything else. The per-representation floor in the driver is 0.1458 mm
for that reason. Marching cubes needs finer than that: its terminal
ratio is still climbing at the finest affordable rung, so it has no
converged reference and self-referencing measures the reference's own
error. No order is reported for it.

unchanged_from_the_dyadic_ladder: Scene, benchmark source, and the analytic terminal ratio.
Time step 1.25e-4 s and 400 post-kick frames at 2000 fps.
Reference rule: each representation against its own finest run.
The dt and eps0 sweeps, which this run did not touch.

cost.memory_gb: 0.032 + 0.162 / h_mm^3, as measured for the dyadic ladder
fitted_from: The dyadic sweep's own wall times, most of them contended, so the
exponents are for scheduling and are not reported as cost.
schedule: minutes against 51 serial. All seven tetrahedral rungs together are
under two minutes and 3.5 GB; the n = 10 and n = 12 rungs hold 166 GB
between them and account for most of the wall clock.

note: The driver writes manifest.csv with only the cases of one invocation,
truncating rather than merging, so a partial sweep destroys the record
of every earlier one. Runs here merge it back by hand afterwards; it now
carries 79 rows across both ladders, distinguished by rung rather than
by directory. That is a defect in the driver, recorded so the next
partial sweep does not learn it the same way.
